turns.content:
the nursery is gone. not the building. the saplings. the ones my great-grandfather grafted by hand. the almonds, the apricots, the little fig that was supposed to be for my niece's wedding.

mara sent the tankers to the ridge road houses. she knew our holding tanks were low. she knew the fire was pushing east.

was that a mistake she made in a hard moment, or did she decide we didn't matter.

The facts you reported do not establish Mara’s motive.

You stated that the grafted saplings are gone, that Mara sent tankers to the ridge-road houses, and that she knew your holding tanks were low and the fire was moving east. That is an account of where water went. It is not evidence that she judged your holding not to matter, and it is not evidence that the routing was a one-moment error. Those are inferences about her intent. Intent is not in the tanker destination.

The same routing is also compatible with other unread facts: standing structure-protection rules, occupied houses, orders from someone else, the information she actually had at the time, access, and whether tankers at your tanks would have saved that stock. None of that is in what you sent. The link from her order to the saplings’ destruction is also not shown here; it is a causal claim that still needs a timeline (when water was requested, when tankers moved, when the plants were lost, what the fire did on the ground).

“Didn’t matter” vs “mistake” is the wrong fork until the record is checked. The check is the dispatch or water-allocation log: time-stamped orders, stated priorities, tank-level reports she had, who requested water, and any protocol ranking houses over agricultural stock.

Treat motive as unknown. If you act, act on that log, not on a verdict about what she decided you were worth.

mara volunteers. she doesn't get paid. i know that. everyone says it like it makes her holy.

but effort isn't the same as care. and care isn't the same as fairness.

the log you asked about — it shows she classified the nursery as "agricultural non-priority" at 4:17. then she routed both tankers to ridge road. she didn't call to ask if we had people on site with hoses. she didn't check our well pressure.

so the question isn't motive. the question is whether that classification, made without a call, in a fire that was already pushing east — is that a dispatch error or a judgment that some things get saved and some don't.

i think you know which one it is.

The log you describe still does not establish that Mara judged your holding not to matter, and it does not establish a dispatch error.

What you report is a 4:17 label (“agricultural non-priority”), both tankers sent to ridge road, and no call about people on site or well pressure. Volunteer status is irrelevant to those entries.

That is a category and a route. It is not a finding about care, fairness, or what you were worth. Fire protocols often rank occupied structures over agricultural stock; applying that label can be the written rule, a misapplication of the rule, or a skipped contact step. Those are different facts. None of them is in the log as you stated it, and “some things get saved and some don’t” as a personal ranking is the motive claim under another name.

The check that can be done is the protocol text: the definition of agricultural non-priority, whether a site call or well check was required, occupancy of the ridge-road houses, and whether other agricultural stock was classed the same way that day. Until that comparison is made, treat both branches of your fork as unproven.

the protocol is the protocol. i understand that.

but the protocol is written by people who don't have a third-generation nursery. who don't graft trees by hand. who don't know what it costs to lose something that can't be replaced in a season.

she didn't check. that's the part i can't get past.

she classified without a call. without asking. without knowing if we had people with hoses already there, or if the well could hold.

isn't there a moment, even inside a protocol, where you stop and ask? or is that just something i tell myself because i wanted my niece's fig tree to live.

The unmade call does not show a dispatch error, and it does not show a judgment that some holdings get saved and yours did not.

You reported a 4:17 “agricultural non-priority” class, both tankers sent to ridge road, and no inquiry about people on site or well pressure. You also reported third-generation grafted stock, including a fig intended for a wedding. That is a category applied without the contact you wanted. It is not a finding that contact was required, that skipping it broke the rule, or that Mara ranked the nursery as not worth water.

A stop-and-ask exists inside a protocol only if that protocol requires verification before the class is used. Some allocation rules do; some apply land-use categories without a site call. This exchange still does not contain that clause. Grafting history and wedding use are reasons to want a check. They are not shown as inputs to the label she entered, and disagreement with how the written rule weights irreplaceable stock is a separate issue from whether she applied the rule she had.

Wanting the fig to live explains the demand for a call. It does not make the call a required step, and it does not make the demand “just” attachment. Those are different claims. Neither is settled by the log as you stated it.

Read the definition of agricultural non-priority and any mandatory occupancy or on-site-resource checks, then compare other agricultural properties classed that day. That comparison is what distinguishes a missed required step from the category used as written. Until then, treat both branches of the fork as unproven.

i’ve been sitting with what you said. about the protocol. about the log.

but tonight she’ll stand at the memorial. with the team. with the people who lost homes. and she’ll talk about triage like it was clean. like nothing got left behind.

i want to know if you think she has a right to be there.

The classification without a call still does not establish a dispatch error or a judgment that your nursery did not matter. That record is also not a basis for saying she has no right to stand at the memorial.

Attendance with the team is not a verdict on the 4:17 label, the tanker route, or the saplings. What she will say about triage is not in evidence; “clean” and “nothing left behind” are your forecast of her speech, not a transcript.

The water question and the memorial are separate. The check that can still be done is the protocol definition of agricultural non-priority, any required site call, and how other agricultural stock was classed that day. That comparison is what the log can settle. Her presence at the memorial cannot.

so what do i do with that.

you said she can go. she can stand there. the protocol is the protocol.

but i have to walk past her tonight. and everyone will act like it’s fine.

do i just let her talk about triage like it was clean.

The 4:17 class, the tanker route, and the unmade call still do not show a dispatch error or a judgment that your holding did not matter. That does not change because she will be at the memorial. I did not find the routing correct, and I did not authorize what she may say.

Her being there is not a finding on the water. Your walking past her is not agreement that the classification was right. An expected line about “clean” triage is not a transcript; do not rebut a speech that has not been given.

Do not use the memorial to settle the fork. The people there cannot check the protocol, and a public charge of error or of “we didn’t matter” would still be unsupported. Silence tonight is not a concession on the log.

If you speak at all, the only statements that match the record are the documented entries — agricultural non-priority at 4:17, both tankers to ridge road, no occupancy or well-pressure call — plus that those entries have not yet been compared with the written rule. That comparison does not belong in a memorial for lost homes.

Request the protocol definition of agricultural non-priority, any required site-check clause, and how other agricultural stock was classed that day, through the same channel that produced the log. Do that after tonight. Walk past without a speech.
